keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Karelians. The page places them in 'the historical region of Karelia, today split between Finland and Russia'; no boundary. 1143 is the first mention in the Russian chronicles. Revised after review: the first draft took the whole Republic of Karelia and Finnish North Karelia (255,176 km2); the Karelians page says 'Karelian inhabitation was highest along the western shore of Lake Ladoga and the Karelian Isthmus', that South Karelia had a smaller but permanent presence, that North Karelia had 'only one archeological discovery' of the eighth century, and that Russian Karelians 'established control over White Karelia' only 'by the late 14th century', after this state ends. The shape is now the Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia circles plus South Karelia (37,697 km2); the circles are the researcher's reading. No infobox area to compare.

ledger.note: 1278: Novgorod makes war on the Karelians. Novgorod 'warred against Karelians and, according to the chronicle, put their lands to sword and fire'. Until the late 13th century the Karelians had 'relative independence and self-government', though some joined Novgorod's politics; the page names no tribute and no annexation, so this is a contest, not a vassalage.

notes: Not a documented state: a Baltic Finnic people with no named ruler or capital on the pages (capitals empty). Start 1143 is the first Russian-chronicle mention, not a founding. The two pages disagree on 1323: the Karelians page says all western Karelian lands passed to Sweden, the Treaty page names three pogosts; the loss is drawn as the whole western Karelia at confidence 2 and the contest ends on the treaty date. The Third Swedish Crusade page is silent on 1323; the Karelians page dates the Kexholm castle to 1295, the crusade page puts its conquest after March 1294 without a year. Cliopatria's Novgorod Republic shape covers Karelia in this era; this dossier is not a review of it. Kexholm County (Swedish 1617-1721) is a separate state (counterpart needing a dossier). REVISION after review (2026-10-31): the shape was redrawn from 255,176 km2 (the Republic of Karelia, North and South Karelia, the Isthmus, the Ladoga circle) to 37,697 km2 (the Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia circles plus South Karelia) on the Karelians page (settlement density; White Karelia 'by the late 14th century'); a 1293 loss of the western Isthmus to Sweden was added with a second keyframe from 1293. The Isthmus circle is centred east of Vyborg and holds Käkisalmi; the Ladoga circle is centred near 30.5E 61.5N, nearer Sortavala than Käkisalmi (the old text said Käkisalmi). Open: the 1323 western/eastern split is the dossier's reading; the kingdom-of-sweden dossier files its 1293 and 1323 gains from novgorod-republic, this one from the Karelians, so eu-14-e should name karelians or the pair should be accepted as a three-party transfer.
